concepts.title: Euclid Division Lemma
concepts.definition: For any two positive integers a and b, there exist unique integers q and r such that a = b*q + r where 0 <= r < b.
concepts.key_idea: Any positive integer can be expressed as a multiple of another integer plus a remainder.
question_patterns: find quotient and remainder using euclid division lemma
apply euclid division algorithm to find hcf
express a in terms of b using division lemma
use euclid lemma to divide integers
find hcf of two numbers using euclid algorithm

solution_steps.explain: Write a = b*q + r with 0 <= r < b.
Replace a with b and b with r; repeat until the remainder becomes 0.
The divisor at the stage where the remainder is 0 is the HCF; the first stage's q and r are the quotient and remainder.

concepts.title: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
concepts.definition: Every composite number can be expressed as a product of primes uniquely, apart from the order of factors.
concepts.key_idea: Prime factorization of a number is unique.

solution_steps.explain: Write every factor as a prime.

concepts.title: Irrationality of sqrt(2)
concepts.definition: The square root of 2 cannot be written as a ratio of two integers, a fact proved by contradiction.
concepts.key_idea: Assuming sqrt(2) = p/q in lowest terms forces both p and q to be even, a contradiction.
question_patterns: prove sqrt(2) is irrational
show that 2 is not a perfect square
prove irrationality of square root of 2
verify that sqrt(2) has non-terminating non-repeating decimal
demonstrate sqrt(2) is not rational

solution_steps.explain: Let sqrt(2) = p/q in lowest terms where p and q are coprime integers.
Squaring gives 2q^2 = p^2, so p^2 is divisible by 2, hence p is divisible by 2. Then q^2 is divisible by 2, hence q is divisible by 2. This contradicts p and q being coprime.
The assumption leads to a contradiction, so sqrt(2) is irrational.

worked_examples.question: Prove that sqrt(2) is irrational.
worked_examples.solution: Assume sqrt(2)=p/q coprime. Then p^2=2q^2 so 2|p; write p=2k, get 4k^2=2q^2 so q^2=2k^2 so 2|q. Contradiction.

concepts.title: Irrationality of sqrt(3) and sqrt(5)
concepts.definition: For any prime p, the square root of p cannot be expressed as a fraction of integers.
concepts.key_idea: The contradiction argument for sqrt(2) extends to the square root of every prime.
question_patterns: prove sqrt(3) is irrational
prove sqrt(5) is irrational
show that 3/sqrt(3) is irrational
prove that 2+sqrt(3) is irrational
prove product of rational and irrational is irrational

solution_steps.explain: Let sqrt(p) = a/b in lowest terms where p is prime.
Then p*b^2 = a^2, so p divides a^2, hence p divides a. Write a = p*k. Then b^2 = p*k^2, so p divides b. Contradiction with coprime assumption.
The contradiction proves sqrt(p) is irrational for prime p.

worked_examples.question: Prove that sqrt(3) is irrational.
worked_examples.solution: Assume sqrt(3)=a/b coprime. Then a^2=3b^2 so 3|a; write a=3k, get 3k^2=b^2 so 3|b. Contradiction.

compute_steps.explain: verify the number-theory claim numerically: lhs = 3 ** 3 + 4 ** 3 gives 91
verify the number-theory claim numerically: diff = 5 ** 3 - lhs gives 34

concepts.title: Decimal Expansion of Rational Numbers
concepts.definition: A simplified fraction terminates as a decimal exactly when its denominator has no prime factors other than 2 and 5.
concepts.key_idea: Look only at the primes in the simplified denominator to predict the decimal's behaviour.
question_patterns: determine if decimal expansion terminates or recurs

classify decimal expansion as terminating or recurring
find number of decimal places in terminating decimal

solution_steps.explain: Cancel common factors so that p and q are coprime.
Write q as a product of primes.
Only 2s and 5s in q give a terminating decimal; any other prime gives a non-terminating recurring decimal.

concepts.title: Terminating Decimal Places
concepts.definition: The number of decimal places in a terminating decimal equals the larger of the powers of 2 and 5 in the simplified denominator.
concepts.key_idea: Scale the denominator to a power of ten; the exponent tells the decimal places.

concepts.title: Properties of Rational and Irrational Numbers
concepts.definition: Combining an irrational number with a non-zero rational by addition, subtraction, multiplication or division always leaves the result irrational.
concepts.key_idea: A rational operand cannot cancel the irrational part unless it is zero.
